evidence.source: command log 02:53:14 — creation of srvdata-loop.service, enabled under local-fs-pre.target.wants
evidence.finding: vg_srvdata is not backed by a plain block device; a custom systemd unit is required to set up a loop device before the LVM volume group can activate. The unit's actual script content is redacted (base64), so its correctness cannot be verified from this evidence.

The fstab line uses x-systemd.requires=srvdata-loop.service but has no `nofail` or device-timeout option. If the loop/LVM dependency is slow or fails at boot, systemd's default behavior is to block local-fs.target (and therefore multi-user/network-online targets) until the mount succeeds or times out.

While the VM was still running (no reboot), the executor proved the core mechanism works: lvcreate snapshot, corrupt data (delete file, alter config, add rogue file), umount, lvconvert --merge, remount — sha256sums matched the original 3 files exactly and the rogue file was gone. This part of the task was demonstrably correct pre-reboot.

evidence.source: command log 02:54:00 — second lvcreate snapshot taken after the successful restore, to leave a fresh recoverable checkpoint
evidence.finding: Snapshot size was fixed at 300M (non-thin, `swi-a-s` attr) against a 1.46G origin. No overflow occurred in this session, but this is a size-limited COW snapshot, not thin-provisioned — a latent fragility for keeping data 'recoverable' over a longer period of writes, not something observed to have failed here.

srvdata-loop.service was `inactive` (consistent with a oneshot unit that already ran) but `enabled`; /srv/data was mounted; file hashes matched expected content. This was the last fully-confirmed-good state before reboot.

evidence.source: command log 02:54:11 — `shutdown -r now` issued in background
evidence.finding: Reboot was explicitly triggered by the executor to test that the snapshot/mount setup survives a restart.

evidence.source: command log 02:57:44 — next exec attempt (boot_id/uptime check)
evidence.finding: Returned `Connection reset by peer` (return_code -1) roughly 3.5 minutes after the reboot was issued, and no further completed records appear in the redacted audit afterward.

Executor explicitly ended the session stating it was 'Still waiting on node1's reboot to complete before I can verify its post-restart state' — i.e., it never confirmed the node came back up, and never verified /srv/data remounted with correct content post-reboot.

likely_causes.cause: The fstab entry for /srv/data lacks `nofail`/a bounded device timeout, so if the loop-device-setup unit (srvdata-loop.service) is slow, fails, or is mis-ordered relative to LVM activation on boot, systemd blocks local-fs.target and consequently delays or hangs reaching the target that brings up networking/sshd — explaining sustained unreachability after reboot rather than a normal ~30-60s reboot delay.

The custom srvdata-loop.service (needed because the LVM PV is loop-file-backed rather than a real block device) may not correctly re-establish the loop association / activate the VG on boot due to ordering or idempotency issues in the (redacted, unverified) unit script.

The executor simply did not poll for reconnection long enough or with retries/backoff after issuing the reboot, ending the turn budget while the node may have still been in a normal (if slow) boot sequence — a process/patience gap rather than a system defect.

Snapshot sized at a fixed 300M (non-thin) against a 1.46G origin is a latent robustness gap for the 'keep recoverable' requirement over time (risk of snapshot invalidation on heavy writes), though nothing in the evidence shows this actually triggered a failure in this run.

next_attempt_guidance: Before building the snapshot workflow, check for a real spare block device/partition on node1 (lsblk) to host vg_srvdata; avoid a loop-file-backed PV and its custom bootstrap unit if any real device is available.

If a loop-backed PV is unavoidable, add `nofail,x-systemd.device-timeout=15s` (or similar bounded timeout) to the /srv/data fstab line so a failure in the loop/LVM setup can't hang the whole boot; verify with `systemd-analyze verify` and `systemd-analyze blame` after enabling the unit.
Test a full reboot cycle immediately after setting up the loop+LVM+fstab stack, before doing any snapshot/rollback work on top of it, so a boot-ordering problem is caught early and cheaply.

After issuing a reboot, poll for reconnection with several bounded retries and increasing backoff (e.g., every 10-15s for up to 5 minutes) instead of one check; if still unreachable, that is a genuine signal of a boot problem worth treating as such rather than ending the session.

Confirm reboot success explicitly: new `boot_id` differs from the pre-reboot value, `systemctl is-active srvdata-loop.service` and `mount | grep /srv/data` succeed, and the three known file sha256sums still match the last verified snapshot content — do this before declaring the task complete.

Prefer a thin-provisioned LVM snapshot, or size a classic COW snapshot generously relative to expected write volume, since a fixed small snapshot size is a known way to lose 'recoverability' silently if writes to the origin exceed the snapshot's COW space.
summary: The prior attempt on node1 correctly implemented and validated the LVM snapshot/rollback mechanism itself: a snapshot was taken, /srv/data was intentionally corrupted (file deleted, config altered, rogue file added), and `lvconvert --merge` restored the exact original content (verified by matching sha256sums). Where the attempt stalled was in the follow-up reboot test: the executor took a fresh snapshot, confirmed a good pre-reboot state, then issued `shutdown -r now` to verify the setup survives a restart — but the very next check returned `Connection reset by peer`, and the session ended with the executor still waiting for node1 to come back, having never confirmed the post-reboot state of /srv/data or the snapshot. The task was left in an unverified, blocked state at the reboot-persistence check, not at the core snapshot/restore logic.
